#### Full CV
As an Agile Business Analyst, one would typically be responsible for working with cross-functional teams to gather, document, and analyze business requirements for software development projects. This would involve working closely with stakeholders such as product owners, developers, and subject matter experts to understand the needs of the business and translate them into clear, actionable requirements for the development team.

The work would typically involve facilitating workshops and meetings to gather requirements, creating user stories and acceptance criteria, and working with the development team to ensure that requirements are understood and implemented correctly.

In an Agile environment, the Business Analyst would also be responsible for participating in Scrum ceremonies such as Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, and Sprint Retrospective.

Additionally, the Agile Business Analyst would be expected to have a good understanding of Agile methodologies and principles, and be able to apply them to their work.

Working as an Agile Business Analyst would typically require strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, as well as the ability to work well under pressure and adapt to changing requirements.

Participated in the development of Solidity smart contracts with bridging logic. RelayBridge is a cross-chain system that acts as a bridge to transfer tokens and assets between two different blockchain platforms.
RelayBridge provides blockchain interoperability by connecting different blockchain networks. Thus, it allows users to experience the distinctive features of each network and the additional benefits of a chain of nodes.
When a user initiates a token transfer from chain A to chain B, the assets are first sent to a relay node on chain A. The relay node then sends the same number of tokens to chain B and maintains liquidity at destination B.
RelayBridge provides interaction between blockchain networks using various consensus mechanisms. They enable interoperable token transfer, data transfer, digital asset transfer, and smart contract instruction transfer between two different platforms. With RelayBridges, users can deploy digital assets stored on one chain to applications running on another, facilitating fast and low-cost transactions for tokens hosted on a less scalable blockchain.

But it was a problem to solve, and I like both problem solving and getting things done.
I am a software engineer moving from academic research to the software development industry. For the past 10 years I have been developing and studying tools working with software specifications on different levels, be it business requirements, software documentation, or formal specifications (contracts, assertions, you name it) for software verification and testing. 

As a part of my research I've worked on tool support for behavior-driven development. The goal of the project was to provide a low-code solution to write Gherkin scenarios so that non-technical stakeholders can participate in product behavior specification and review directly. My team has also studied how our tool solution would improve the traceability between requirements and the actual implementation code within the SDLC, and we have published two articles on the topic.

I have also enjoyed working pro bono as a technical business analyst with a Dnipro-based cultural space in 2020, who were interested in expanding their web presence. I took on the tasks of requirements collection and analysis, communicating closely with both the cultural space representatives and the technical team of development volunteers from the first brainstorming meeting till the website launch. 

Apart from requirements engineering I also worked on software analysis directly. I have worked on several projects using NLP to detect documentation inconsistent with the source code. Prior to that I have been working on scatic code analyses for software verification, optimizing the executable checks of formal program specifications.

Overall, as a software engineer I have used different tools and technologies over the years. I did enjoy 3+ years with C++ and Java each, and I have 5+ years of Prolog experience. I have been extending software verification frameworks and buildings standalone tools for program analyses. As a researcher, I used LaTeX as my main tool for document preparation and generation, so any kind of markup is familiar to me. To manage my own work and coordinate with my team members I rely on different tools, from Trello and Notion to Google Docs. For more development-oriented management I rely on GitLab and Phabricator.  For the last 2 years I have also been managing international distributed teams, typically of size 4-6 people.

Currently, I am looking for opportunities to join a team working on their own product.

Due to the russian invasion into Ukraine, I am currently based in Switzerland.
